claims.subject: CPython robustness contribution
claims.value: repeated and externally visible upstream bug-reporting activity
claims.boundary: This supports sustained participation in CPython robustness work, not ownership of CPython or independent authorship of every analysis/fix.

claims.subject: Python fuzzing tools
claims.value: substantial project implementation/maintenance is evidenced for lafleur and labeille; fusil is maintenance/revival work
claims.boundary: Repository ownership and detailed documentation do not establish independent implementation of every subsystem; fusil has explicit upstream lineage.

claims.subject: Bug reproduction and verification
claims.value: repeated human review, re-reproduction and source verification are explicitly documented
claims.boundary: AI assistance is substantial in drafting, reduction and parts of investigation; the supported human role is review/verification/judgment, not unaided production.

claims.subject: Bug reproduction and verification
claims.value: repeated crash/race reproduction, negative controls and build comparisons are present across multiple CPython reports
claims.boundary: The evidence is strongest inside CPython robustness campaigns and should not be generalized to arbitrary systems debugging.

claims.subject: AI-assisted development
claims.value: Claude Code is explicitly part of catalog assembly, report drafting, reproducer reduction and review tooling
claims.boundary: Assistance must not erase the subject's explicitly documented reviewing, re-reproducing and source-checking roles.

claims.subject: CPython JIT testing
claims.value: author/maintainer context and detailed tools show sustained JIT fuzzing/test infrastructure work
claims.boundary: This does not by itself prove independent compiler/JIT implementation expertise.

claims.subject: Free-threaded CPython testing
claims.value: repeated TSan/free-threading investigation and verification across multiple race classes
claims.boundary: The evidence supports CPython-specific concurrency testing and triage, not broad independent concurrency design mastery.

claims.subject: OOM and allocation-failure testing
claims.value: repeated OOM injection, crash deduplication, reproduction and disclosure workflow
claims.boundary: AI-assisted reductions/writeups mean independent derivation of every root cause remains unresolved.

claims.subject: AI-assisted CPython code review
claims.value: a structured Claude Code plugin and campaign workflow exists for CPython-specific review
claims.boundary: Do not translate this into fully manual C code-review mastery; candidate generation and report drafting are explicitly agent-assisted.

claims.subject: Python ecosystem compatibility testing
claims.value: labeille implements package resolution, real test-suite execution, bisect, benchmarks, free-threading and extension compatibility workflows
claims.boundary: This supports tool/workflow implementation in this project, not expertise in every third-party package.

claims.subject: Fuzzing campaign operations
claims.value: campaign aggregation, deduplication, triage registries and impact accounting recur across lafleur and bug catalogs
claims.boundary: Some catalog/tool assembly is explicitly AI-assisted; independent implementation depth varies by artifact.

claims.subject: Upstream contribution workflow
claims.value: issues, proposed fixes, linked PR artifacts and long-running triage history are central to the public footprint
claims.boundary: Linked PRs are not automatically attributable to the subject without per-PR validation.

claims.subject: CPython C internals
claims.value: repeated source-level investigations show meaningful working exposure and bounded understanding of CPython internals
claims.boundary: The snapshot does not establish broad independent C implementation mastery across CPython.

claims.subject: Python ecosystem reliability
claims.value: reliability/bug finding is a recurring theme across owned tools, CPython reports and self-described goals
claims.boundary: Representativeness is not a global skill score and does not imply equivalent depth across all Python projects.
